Saving to—

Photos are written here as they are taken, so nothing is lost if the app closes. Exports go here too.

Use it as an app

On an iPhone or iPad, add Site Capture to the Home Screen and open it from that icon. It then works without a signal and keeps your photos. Projects started in a Safari tab stay in that tab.

Exports

In a browser, an export opens the share menu: on an iPhone choose Save to Files, AirDrop or Mail. On a computer it goes to your Downloads folder. Photos stay inside the browser until you export them, so export often.

Reports

Your colours, logo, cover title and a footer line on every page of the PDF report. Needs a license or subscription.

Help

A walkthrough of every feature, from the first photo to the finished export.

Your version

Your own templates need a license or subscription. Capture and export are the same on every version.

Asset Match (AI photo sorter)

On device
Gemini

On device reads any text in the photo and works offline with no key, but it cannot tell what an unlabelled thing is. Gemini looks at the picture itself and is far better on assets with nothing written on them. Gemini needs a signal and a key — and a key is free.

Google AI Studio issues a key on a free tier that covers normal survey use — no card, no subscription. Sign in, tap Create API key, then paste it above. Heavy use can exceed the free limits, which Google publishes on the same page.

Pro

Lite

Matches an unfiled photo to the assets in this project. The key is stored on this phone, never sent anywhere but Google, and only used when Gemini is selected.

Build a template from Excel
Four tabs describe your survey; the fourth is optional. Start from the example file.

Replace the example rows with your own, then choose the file below.

Tab 1
Project Information
Recorded once per project.
Field nameTypeOptionsDefault
ClientText
Surveyed byTextA. Surveyor
Building typeDropdownOffice, Retail, School
Default is what the field starts with. Here it can only be plain text — there is nothing else for it to read from yet.
Tab 2
Asset List
One row per asset. Repeat the category as often as you need — this tab cannot be empty.
CategoryAssetUnit PriceTypical Defects
RoofingMain roof membrane85Blisters, Ponding, Split seams
RoofingCap flashing40Loose fixings, Corrosion
MechanicalRooftop unit8000Corroded casing, Worn belts
Two more columns are optional: Subcategory and Code. Anything you add after those — Unit Price and Typical Defects above — travels with the asset. It shows behind the (i) beside the asset name, and a data field can read from it by name.
Tab 3
Data Fields
Filled in for every photo.
Field nameTypeOptionsMergeDefault
ConditionSelectGood, Fair, PoorUnique
QuantityNumberSum
Unit costTextUnique[Unit Price]
Defects seenSelect multipleUnique[Typical Defects]
Desk reviewh_Text areaUnique
Merge is optional — Unique says a repeated answer once, All keeps every one, Sum adds numbers up. Blank uses the sensible default for the type.
Field nameRelevant
Condition
RefrigerantMechanical
Seam conditionMain roof membrane
Relevant is optional too — the categories a field belongs to, comma separated. The field then shows only on photos of those categories, so a furnace and a window can each have their own questions. Leave it blank and the field shows on every photo. An asset's own name or subcategory works as well.
A field that already holds an answer always shows, so filing a photo somewhere else never hides what was written on it.
Default can be plain text, or a name in [square brackets]. The name is looked up in your Project Information first, then in the asset's own columns — so [Unit Price] gives every asset its own figure, ready to be edited.
Defaults can calculate, live. A sum in round brackets is worked out again every time anything on the photo's form changes: ([Unit Price] * [Quantity]) follows the quantity as it is counted on site. It reads the form's own fields first, then the project information, then the asset's row — so a name that is both a column and a field takes the one being typed into. Use + − * / and brackets. Ordinary text in brackets is left alone, and a sum whose figures are missing comes out blank.
A default that reads a column can only be filled in once there is an asset to read. Photograph something unfiled and file it afterwards and the figures arrive then — filing the photo fetches them. The ↻ beside the field asks for them again at any time.
Correct a calculated figure by hand and it stays corrected — the formula stops touching it. Tap ↻ beside the field (or empty the box) to hand it back to the formula.
A formula may read another calculated field — a cost feeds a tax feeds a total — and the Asset summary recalculates too, so changing a quantity there moves the total. Anything the summary recalculates is marked Edited; the row's ↻ puts the photo merge back.
Brackets nest as deep as you need: (([Useful Life]+[Year Installed])-[Assessment Year]) gives years remaining. Only + − * / are understood — no percentages, powers or functions — and a unit written after a figure is ignored, so 42 m2 counts as 42. If any figure a sum needs is missing, the whole sum comes out blank rather than a part-answer.
On a Select, Dropdown or Select multiple, the default becomes the choices rather than the answer. [Typical Defects] above means a roof offers roofing defects and a rooftop unit offers its own.
Put h_ in front of the type — h_Text area — for a field that is filled from the asset list rather than at the camera, for answers that take longer than a photo allows.
Tab 4
General Notes — optional
The skeleton the project's General notes opens with. One line per row, in the first column — headings, prompts, a running order.
A
SITE OVERVIEW
Weather and access on the day:
CONDITION SUMMARY
Items needing attention within 12 months:
It fills an empty notes box only, so nothing written on site is ever replaced. Leave the tab out and the notes box simply starts blank, as before.
Edit it later on the phone under ⋯ → General Notes Template, and it travels with Export template.
Types you can use
Text — a single line Number — digits only Text area — several lines Select — tap one of a few buttons Dropdown — pick from a long list Select multiple — tick several
These three need choices — in Options, comma separated, or from a Default that names a column. Select multiple writes what you tick as it reads: Blisters, Ponding and Split seams.
A Default naming options the field already has is the answer, not a new list: Good on a Good/Fair/Poor field starts every photo on Good and leaves the three choices alone. Select multiple takes several. A default naming anything else — a column, or wording not in Options — becomes the option list instead.
You do not have to think of every option now. On the phone, Select multiple has an Add box and a dropdown has a ✎; anything added on site is offered on the photos that follow.
Good to know
Tabs are found by name, or by order if renamed. The file name becomes the template name. Any other column on the Asset List becomes asset information, shown behind the (i) beside the asset name and available to a [Default] by that column's heading.
Nothing here is compulsory. A sheet with just Field name and Type still imports, exactly as before.
